The dollar ceiling on the pre-clearance exemption for same-day trades in common stock of issuers with a market capitalization of at least $10 billion was lowered from $25,000 to $10,000.
A carve-out was added to the exchange-traded fund exemption: ETFs seeking a leveraged or inverse multiple of the daily return of an index are no longer exempt and now require pre-clearance.
The Code of Ethics quarterly transaction report deadline was shortened from thirty (30) to fifteen (15) calendar days after the end of each calendar quarter.

The exception from Gift Log recording for logo promotional items under $50, shared perishable food and modest seminar or due diligence meals was deleted, so every gift and entertainment event must now be logged under Section 3.2.
Reimbursement of client losses caused by trade error corrections changed from discretionary (the Firm may reimburse) to mandatory (the Firm shall reimburse).
The definition of complaint was expanded from written statements only to written or oral statements, bringing oral complaints within the one-business-day reporting and complaint log requirements.

New off-channel communications policy limiting written business communications to Approved Channels (Firm email, client portal, archived messaging on Firm-issued devices, approved social media accounts), prohibiting personal email, personal texts, WhatsApp, Signal and personal social media, and requiring any off-channel business message received to be preserved and reported to the CCO within one business day, with quarterly certification.

New incident response program under amended Regulation S-P requiring notice to affected individuals as soon as practicable and no later than 30 days after the Firm becomes aware of unauthorized access, and service provider notice to the Firm within 72 hours of a breach.
The approval authority for outside business activities moved from the Compliance Committee to the CCO.

New procedure requiring wealth advisors to request a trusted contact person from each natural person client at account opening and each annual review, and requiring escalation of suspected diminished capacity or financial exploitation to the CCO within one business day.

The insider trading prohibition, which extended only to the issuer's own debt, swaps and other derivatives, now also covers the securities of any other issuer (such as a competitor, supplier or acquirer) whose price the information could reasonably be expected to affect.
Authority to remove an issuer from the Restricted List moves from any member of the Compliance Department to the CCO alone, who must make the removal determination.

New expert network policy: expert network firms must be CCO-approved, each consultation must be pre-cleared one business day ahead, current insiders, recent (under six months) departees and government employees may not be consulted, calls open with a compliance script and are chaperoned on a sample basis.
The pre-clearance approval window is shortened from the close of regular trading on the business day following approval to the close of regular trading on the day of approval.
The minimum holding period for Reportable Securities acquired in a Covered Account is lengthened from 30 to 60 calendar days.

The exemption from pre-clearance and the minimum holding period for common stock of issuers with a market capitalization above $10 billion, up to $25,000 per issuer in any rolling 30 calendar days, is deleted.

A carve-out is added to the exclusion for losses caused by an executing broker or counterparty: the exclusion no longer applies where the broker or counterparty acted on inaccurate or incomplete instructions from the Adviser, so the Adviser now reimburses those losses.

New short sale policy requiring Regulation SHO locates recorded in the order management system and barring Fund purchases in firm commitment offerings after short sales in the Rule 105 restricted period absent written CCO confirmation of an exception.

Approval of valuation overrides moves from the Chief Financial Officer alone to the Valuation Committee, acting by a majority of its voting members that must include the CCO, and no override may be applied until the Committee approves it in writing.
Pre-clearance of state and local political contributions by Covered Associates changes from optional ('may seek pre-clearance') to mandatory ('must obtain pre-clearance').

Adds a sentence that market-driven changes such as equity market declines can reduce client demand for margin lending, which is newly described as a significant source of net interest revenue.

The Company now says it extensively utilized higher-cost funding sources to support the 2022 and 2023 client cash reallocation (previously it utilized higher-cost supplemental funding sources), and client cash is recast from something the Company relies heavily on to generate revenue into a significant funding source for revenue.

The rate-sensitive interest-earning assets expand from investment securities and mortgages to investment securities plus margin loans, mortgages, and PALs, and market conditions is dropped as a stated driver of higher deposit rates, leaving only the competitive environment.

Custody is added to the relationships that interconnect financial institutions, and further FDIC premium increases or special assessments are now tied to potential future bank failures or other similar events rather than only to the cost of resolving the 2023 bank failures (heading reworded to 'direct adverse effects').
Adds a new data exposure risk from failure to adequately destroy data during system or asset decommissioning, which could make client or Company information available to external parties in error.

Covers reliance on external service providers for key technology, cloud infrastructure, processing, servicing, support and custody functions, and on financial intermediaries, where their failure to perform could cause losses and reputational harm to Schwab and financial harm to clients.

Covered reliance on outsourced service providers for key technology, cloud, processing, servicing and support functions, and the risk that their failures, data misuse or service interruptions (including past outages and COVID-19 service losses) disrupt operations and cause losses.

Covers losses from fraud and financial crime, including account takeover through social engineering, phishing and AI-enabled impersonation, fraudulent money movement and account openings, deliberate client fraud, employee insider misconduct, and losses reimbursed under Schwab's guarantee against unauthorized account activity.

Covered reliance on market makers, dealers, exchanges, clearing houses and other intermediaries to execute and settle client orders, and on payments from market makers and exchanges for trade execution and from securities lending counterparties as a significant source of revenue.
